versions.short: The bill would require several federal financial regulators, including the Federal Reserve Board, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, the FDIC, the Treasury Department, the Comptroller of the Currency, FinCEN, the Federal Housing Finance Agency, and the National Credit Union Administration, to review the technology they use to oversee the businesses they supervise and whether that technology can support real-time supervisory assessments. The bill would also require these agencies to review the rules and steps they follow when buying or building new technology systems and to look for ways to make those procedures faster and simpler. Every five years, each agency would have to report to specified congressional committees on its supervisory technology and planned upgrades, its purchasing practices, its technology development staff, and how it shares data.
